entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:1
segments: How beautiful [are] your feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! The curves of your thighs [are] like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:2
segments: Your navel [is like] a round goblet, which never lacks mixed wine; your belly [is like] a heap of wheat set about with lilies.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:3
segments: Your two breasts [are] like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:4
segments: Your neck [is like] a tower of ivory; your eyes [like] the fish-pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Beth-rabbim; your nose [is like] the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:5
segments: Your head on you [is like] Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple cloth; the King [is] held captive in its tresses.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:6
segments: How beautiful and how pleasant you [are], O love, for delights!

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:7
segments: Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts [are] like clusters [of grapes].

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:8
segments: I said, I will go up in the palm tree, I will take hold of its stalk. And please let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the smell of your nose like apples;

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:9
segments: and the roof of your mouth like the best wine for my Beloved, that goes [down] smoothly for My Beloved, flowing softly [over] the lips of sleeping ones.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:10
segments: I [am] my Beloved's, and His desire [is] toward me.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:11
segments: Come, my Beloved, let us go out into the field; let us stay in the villages.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:12
segments: Let us rise up early to the vineyards; let us see [if] the vine flowers, whether the tender grape appears, and the pomegranates bud forth; there I will give You my loves.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:13
segments: The love-apples give a scent, and over our doors [are] all pleasant [fruits], new and old, which I have laid up for You, O my Beloved.
